subject: china-studies
title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades

segments.say: Start with the map at the first stage. The map is mostly farmland, a small town stands where the roads cross, and only 15 of every 100 people live in the town - the urban share is 15 and the rural share is 85. Point at both share bars on your student notes before anything is built.
questions: What covers most of the map at the first stage?
What are the urban and rural shares at this stage?

segments.say: Build the second stage at the edge. Factories are built on farmland at the town edge, their jobs pull people in from the countryside, and the first housing blocks rise beside the factories as the urban share climbs to 38. Now try the stage 2 question on your worksheet.
questions: What is built first at the edge, and why do people move in?
How far does the urban share climb at this stage?

segments.say: Spread the city outward. The built-up districts spread from the core and the factories, the farmland shrinks to a strip in the west, and most people now live in the city - the urban share reaches 62 and the rural share falls to 38. Check both shares against your student notes before moving on.
questions: From where do the districts spread outward?
Why does the rural share fall by the same amount the urban share climbs?

segments.say: The sudden leap, then the correction. Played as one leap, the farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once - but the replay shows the true order: factories and housing at the edge, districts spreading outward, shares moving at every stage, until the city is mostly built-up with an urban share of 85. Keep the four stages in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What does the sudden-leap version leave out?
What are the urban and rural shares at the final stage?
segments.watchFor: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once. Listen for students who treat the two end photographs as a single step. Send them back to the stages: Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in: factories and the first housing blocks are built on farmland at the edge as migrants arrive for jobs, the built-up districts then spread outward stage by stage, and the urban population share climbs - and the rural share falls - at every stage until the city is mostly built-up.
